subject: Renewal: elastic reserve credit proposal & burst fallback handshake
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@brightpay.com>, BrightPay Procurement <procurement@brightpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: elastic reserve credit proposal & burst fallback handshake

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our call, BrightPay is planning to renew the Dedicated pool and add 24 GPUs for Q3 to support payroll seasonality. You raised two items I promised to follow up on: (1) how burst capacity will behave during sustained peaks, and (2) options to keep unit economics predictable if you need occasional on-demand lift.

We sketched an idea internally I wanted to run by you: an "Elastic Reserve Credit" (ERC) bucket layered on top of the reserved pool. High level: you keep the committed GPUs (24 additional) for guaranteed baseline throughput and a 72-hr 99th percentile latency SLO on those instances. Separately, an ERC bucket provides short-duration burst capacity (on-demand GPUs) that drains credits rather than instantly charging high overage rates.

Benefits for BrightPay: predictable cost for occasional spikes, a safety net for short sustained peaks, and explicit fallback behavior when ERC is exhausted (soft-fallback to reduced throughput vs hard reject).

Would you and procurement be open to a short (30 min) session next week to walk the mechanics and numbers? I attached a one-page matrix and a draft amendment to the renewal that maps credits to GPU-hours.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: elastic-reserve-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: draft-amendment-v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@brightpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: elastic reserve credit proposal & burst fallback handshake

Marcus —

Thanks for the concise summary. A few clarifying questions before we schedule:

1) When ERC is active, is the latency SLO (72-hr 99th) still guaranteed for requests that land on the reserved pool, or do bursts affect that SLA?
2) Can you define the fallback behavior when ERC is exhausted? We prefer a throttled queued-mode that lets critical payroll requests proceed (albeit slower) rather than a hard reject.
3) How do credits translate to cost — e.g., is 1 GPU-hour of ERC the same dollar rate as a reserved GPU-hour or somewhere between reserved and on-demand?

Procurement would also like a short worked example of a payroll-week spike vs a sustained 48-hour incident so they can model TCO. Procurement cc'd on this email: procurement@brightpay.com.

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightPay

Subject: Re: Renewal: elastic reserve credit proposal & burst fallback handshake

Folks —

Quick internal note before we reply to BrightPay with a formal MAM and numbers. High-level proposal (we should run these by legal/pricing):

- Baseline: 24 extra reserved GPUs added to BrightPay's pool; price = committed rate per GPU-hour as in existing contract.
- ERC model: sell a bucket of credits (monthly or annual pre-bought) where 1 credit = 1 GPU-hour of burst capacity on compatible hardware. Credits can be consumed only for bursts that exceed baseline.
- Pricing: credits priced at 1.6x reserved rate (midway between reserved and on-demand) if bought annually; 1.9x if purchased monthly. The goal is to not convert ERC into an excuse for constant overages — include a volume breakpoint where we recommend moving to more reserved capacity.
- Fallback behavior: when ERC > 0, requests spill to ERC seamlessly; when ERC = 0, we provide a configurable soft-fallback: (A) degraded-QoS routing (queue + priority for critical paths) for up to 24 hours, then (B) circuit-break to on-demand marketplace with customer approval. No transparent hard-reject unless customer explicitly chooses hard cap.
- Guarantees: baseline reserved GPUs keep the 72-hr 99th latency SLO. ERC-supplied GPUs are best-effort for the SLO but we will surface per-token latency percentiles and explain variance in the MAM.

Next steps for us: build two worked examples (payroll-week spike; 48-hr incident) and attach a proposed amendment draft. Marcus — can you schedule a 30-min walkthrough with BrightPay and procurement? Dev — once you have language, put the amendment in track-changes.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success

[Attachment: proposal-notes.txt (txt)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: draft amendment (v2) & ERC contract language

Marcus / Marissa —

Attached: draft-amendment-v2.pdf and an ERC pricing matrix. Key contract snippets below (for legal):

-- Contract snippet start --
Elastic Reserve Credits (ERC): Customer may elect to purchase ERC in advance. One ERC equals one GPU-hour of burst execution capacity. ERC are consumed only when customer usage exceeds the committed reserved pool. ERC will be billed as a pre-paid bucket; unused credits do not carry a refund unless otherwise agreed.

Fallback Behavior: While ERC remain, Redwood will route overflow to ERC resources. When ERC are exhausted, Redwood will route to the configured soft-fallback mode (degraded throughput with prioritized request queues). Customer may opt-in to automatic marketplace on-demand purchase as a hard fallback; absent opt-in, Redwood will throttle non-critical requests and notify customer.

Throughput & SLA: Reserved GPUs remain subject to the baseline 72-hour 99th percentile latency SLO. ERC-executed work is considered burst capacity and is not covered by the baseline SLO; Redwood will publish post-incident latency metrics.
-- Contract snippet end --

I've added redlines in draft-amendment-v2.pdf. Also attached the elastic-reserve-matrix.xlsx with worked examples (payroll-week and 48-hr incident).

Let me know if this is safe to send to BrightPay procurement; if so I'll attach the amendment in DocuSign and share the MAM link.

Dev
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: elastic reserve credit proposal & burst fallback handshake

Emily / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clarifying questions; quick answers inline and a proposal for next steps:

1) SLA impact: reserved GPUs retain the 72-hr 99th latency SLO. ERC is intended for bursts; while we try to hit similar latency on ERC-backed capacity, those instances are not contractually covered by the reserved SLO. We'll share post-incident reports for visibility.

2) Fallback behavior: by default we propose the soft-fallback path — degraded throughput with prioritized queues for critical endpoints (payroll submit, batch settle). If you prefer a hard cap we can add an opt-in checkbox in the amendment.

3) Credit economics: see attached matrix. Example: payroll-week worked example shows how 200 ERC (GPU-hours) would cost ~1.6x the committed rate but keep peak spend predictable versus raw on-demand.

Next steps:
- We will send the DocuSign amendment (draft-amendment-v2) with the ERC section and a checkbox for automatic marketplace opt-in.
- Schedule 30-min walkthrough: Mon 24 May 2027 10:00 AM ET (I included a Calendly link in the MAM).
- Procurement: please confirm if you want automatic marketplace opt-in or prefer manual approval when ERC is exhausted.

Link: [MAM: https://app.redwood.com/mam/BP-8247]

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll have the DocuSign ready and attach the worked examples.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
